Frozen Go's ARC sealing signed with columns the active schema lacks, never authenticated the incoming chain (any ARC-Seal gave cv=pass), scanned bodies for instances and let the counter wrap. Rust seals through mail-auth with the active key and verifies the chain. The seal now uses the RECEIVING (recipient's hosted) domain's key, never the attacker-controlled From-header domain; with no key for the receiving domain nothing is sealed.

reason: Frozen Go matched PKIX-TA (usage 0) against any certificate in the peer chain, including the leaf, with no check that the matched CA is in the validated chain. Rust requires a CA certificate (presented or trusted) that the leaf verifies against, in addition to ordinary PKIX; a leaf-only association no longer matches.

Frozen Go looked the TLSA RRset up twice (before connecting and again after the handshake) and decided on the second answer; a failed second lookup rejected a session the first answer validated. Rust decides once, from the answer used for the pool decision and the handshake verifier, so a record that changes between two lookups cannot split the decision.
mutant: none: single-answer decision, covered by the linkage cases

reason: Go reused a pooled TLS session as DANE-validated although no TLSA record had matched it. Rust marks a session DANE-validated only after a record matched its chain and re-checks the current records on reuse. The recorded case still replays (Rust performs one TLSA lookup per delivery, so its third recorded answer is never consumed); the bug itself is asserted by pool-session-without-a-matching-record-is-not-reused in secfix-transport.json.

owner-approved security fix 2026-11-05: Frozen Go picked the first enabled local attendee named in the iMIP body and wrote a tentative event into that tenant's calendar although the envelope recipient was another tenant (unauthenticated cross-tenant calendar write). Rust accepts only an attendee that owns the mailbox the delivered envelope recipient resolves to; the recorded delivery now imports no event.

owner-approved security fix 2026-11-05: Frozen Go's iMIP verified the signed body without the revocation blocklist, so a revoked or blocklisted signer's CANCEL still removed events while the message badge said untrusted. Rust passes the revocation option: the revoked signer is graded untrusted and iMIP stops.

owner-approved security fix 2026-11-05: Frozen Go verified a multipart/signed message whose extra unsigned part followed the closing boundary and kept the valid verdict (badge, iMIP, no link rewriting or phish warning for that part). Rust refuses to grade a message with parts outside the signed pair as signed: no verdict, the message is processed like unsigned mail and iMIP does not trust the signed CANCEL.

owner-approved security fix 2026-11-05: Frozen Go answered an anti-phishing-only rejection with 250 OK and silently dropped the mail (sender and recipient never learn it was lost). Rust replies 550 Message rejected per anti-phishing policy.

owner-approved security fix 2026-11-05: A second lowercase Content-Type frames an unsigned multipart/mixed part in the signed message's preamble (a parser differential between the S/MIME extractor and the body walkers). Rust picks the boundary like the walkers, refuses a second Content-Type and any preamble text, so the message is unsigned mail and the part's link is rewritten.
